title: The LCLI-469 handshake must name the schema regeneration a lore pin bump needs, not only the skills baseline
description:
From the 0.13.0 release, found by opum-marketplace on opum-ai/opum-marketplace#201 and hit again by opum-cli-e2e on opum-ai/opum-cli-e2e#394.

Moving a consumer lore pin to 0.13.0 turned its `lore check` red with exit 6. The eleven schema-drift errors were ten stale x-lore-generator.profileDigest stamps plus a new Standard document type with no committed schema. The LCLI-469 handshake the release sends — the four values in the prompt and in docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md item 8, and the block scripts/promote-latest.mjs prints as post-latest checklist item 4 — said only "carry the re-resolved skills baseline". That is necessary and NOT sufficient: a pin bump also moves the OKF schema surface, so the consumer must regenerate its committed schemas in the same change.

The tool-prescribed fix, which worked for opum-marketplace, is `lore schema export` run under the NEW lore (`npx --yes @opum-ai/lore@0.13.0`), committed with the pin bump.

This does not block LCLI-665; it is a defect in the handshake template that release hands out.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The LCLI-469 handshake — both the printed post-latest checklist item and the runbook text — names the schema regeneration a lore pin bump needs, not only the skills baseline, so a consumer that pins a new lore version does not discover the drift by going red
